statement: A person who left home between 4 p.m. and 5 p.m. returned between 5 p.m. and 6 p.m. and found that the hands of his watch had exactly exchanged places. When did he go out?

Solve the system:
\[
\begin{cases}
\log_2 x + \log_4 y + \log_4 z = 2 \\
\log_3 y + \log_9 z + \log_9 x = 2 \\
\log_4 z + \log_{16} x + \log_{16} y = 2
\end{cases}
\]

Two circles with radii $a$ and $b$ respectively touch each other externally. Let $c$ be the radius of a circle that touches these two circles as well as a common external tangent to the two circles. Prove that
\[
\frac{1}{\sqrt{c}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{a}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{b}}.
\]
Find the least natural number whose last digit is $7$ such that it becomes $5$ times larger when this last digit is carried to the beginning of the number.
If $P(x)$ is a polynomial with integer coefficients and $a, b, c$ are three distinct integers, then show that it is impossible to have $P(a) = b$, $P(b) = c$, $P(c) = a$.
Construct a quadrilateral which is not a parallelogram, in which a pair of opposite angles and a pair of opposite sides are equal.
If $a, b, x, y$ are integers greater than $1$ such that $a$ and $b$ have no common factor except $1$ and $x^a = y^b$, show that $x = n^b$, $y = n^a$ for some integer $n$ greater than $1$.

Suppose $A_1, \ldots, A_6$ are six sets each with four elements and $B_1, \ldots, B_n$ are $n$ sets each with two elements. Let $S = A_1 \cup A_2 \cup \cdots \cup A_6 = B_1 \cup \cdots \cup B_n$. Given that each element of $S$ belongs to exactly four of the $A$'s and to exactly three of the $B$'s, find $n$.
Show that among all quadrilaterals of a given perimeter the square has the largest area.
